metadataReview.note: Reviewed location: the cited English and Russian Wikipedia revisions place the battle of 12 August 1812 (31 July Old Style) at Gorodechno, then a small town in Kobrinsky uyezd and now in Pruzhany District, Brest Region, where Tormasov held a defensive position behind a marshy tributary of the Mukhavets. Two encyclopaedias transcribed on Wikisource name the same place. The Brockhaus–Efron dictionary (1893) places the battle of 31 July 1812 (Julian) at Gorodechna in Kobrin uyezd, Grodno governorate. The Sytin Military Encyclopedia (1911–1915) sets Tormasov's position on the heights along the right bank of the small Gorodechna river, with the Bolshoye Poddubye crossing 4 versts west of the town. The English Wikipedia revision gives infobox coordinates 52°25′25.37″N 24°18′35.92″E, about 30 m from the stored point. The point is the gazetteer position of that village (Belarusian Гарадзечна). It is a sector reference for the Russian position named by the sources, not Schwarzenberg's detachment turning the Russian left, the allied attack positions or the full battlefield. The existing date is retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: GeoNames 628204, Haradzyechna (alternate names Gorodechno, Гарадзечна) in Brest Region, publishes latitude 52.4235 and longitude 24.3099. The OSM hamlet boundary Гарадзечна in Pruzhany District (relation 7467844) has its Nominatim centre at 52.4238513, 24.3101915, about 45 m away, confirming this is the Pruzhany District village and not the homonyms in Navahrudak or Valozhyn districts. Stored as [24.3099,52.4235]. This is a village reference for the Russian defensive position, not a surveyed line, a dam crossing or any regiment's position, and it does not represent the detachment sent round the Russian left through the forest. No positional accuracy radius is claimed.
